title: Domino's Analysis: Value Stock or Value Trap? | DPZ Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc weighs Domino's after it secured the top slot on Uber Eats and DoorDash, with management reporting record order frequency but a falling average order value — the near-term worry. The long-term record impresses him: sales more than doubled from under $2.5B (2017) to over $5B TTM, holding up even after the pandemic reopening, which he reads as proof of the customer value proposition (chapter one of his investing book). Unit economics (chapter two) are elite: 19.3% operating margin near decade highs and 51% ROIC against a sub-15% WACC, powered by the franchise model. Valuation is the kicker: forward P/E of 14.72 is near the cheapest in years, depressed by macro headwinds (higher rates lifting the opportunity cost of capital, squeezed consumer disposable income), and his DCF values the business at $326 — about 6% above the market price. Verdict: a genuine value stock, not a trap. Call: DPZ BUY at ~$307 (first tracked call on the name).

calls.thesis: Forward P/E 14.72 near cheapest in years; 19.3% operating margin, 51% ROIC; best value proposition in QSR; DCF $326 ~6% above current price. First tracked call.
calls.bull_case: Top-of-app on Uber Eats/DoorDash drives order frequency higher.
calls.bear_case: Average order value falling; squeezed consumer trades down.
